Frozen food began with a fish on the ice. In Labrador in 1912, fur trader Clarence Birdseye watched Inuit fishermen leave their catch on the ice, where it froze at once and tasted fresh when cooked later.

Frozen food in shops was mush, because it froze slowly and grew large ice crystals. Birdseye copied the cold and built a freezer that pressed food between chilled belts. His first company ran out of money. He kept going, and in 1930 his frozen food reached the shops of Springfield, Massachusetts.

Home refrigerators rose from under 10 percent of American homes to over 50.
